decisions.reason: Publishing on the assigned page is consistent with the existing dedicated-account state; sending the published link does not change the account's setup, profile, or audience-routing requirements.
Sending a published-post link to the client does not change which clips or performance metrics must be tracked.
Directly sending the post link to the client is distinct from recording the posting date and Reel link in Notion and does not resolve the unspecified Notion destination.
The source changes link reporting after publication but does not alter the one-per-day cadence or the 6 PM to 9 PM posting window.
The instruction to send a published-post link does not change the caption, hashtags, tagged account, tag placement, or unresolved handle choice.
The post-link reporting instruction does not change the deferred monthly quota or its target of 100 approved clips.
The source concerns publishing and link delivery after approval; it does not change approval authority, eligibility, correction, or quota-counting rules.
Posting these clips on the assigned page does not remove or otherwise change the established target-channel set.
Publication and link reporting do not affect the requirement for background music, its volume, or mood-based selection.
The instruction applies to current approved-clip publication and does not alter the already completed initial three-clip trial.
The publishing destination and post-link reporting instruction do not change permissible source material or moment-selection rules.
The source does not change the 45-to-60-second duration range or the 45-second approval minimum.
